request.spec:
When a claim is opened it receives the next number on the sheet: 1 for the first claim ever
opened on the sheet, then 2, and so on, with no gaps and never reused, even when two users open
claims at the same moment. A draft has no number, and voiding a claim clears its number (the
number is not given to anyone else). Show the number on the claim. Every audit line about a
claim that has a number gains number=<number> at its end (so CLAIM_OPENED and CLAIM_SETTLED
carry it; a CLAIM_VOIDED line carries the number the claim had).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
When a claim is opened it receives the next number on the sheet: 1 for the first claim ever
opened on the sheet, then 2, and so on, with no gaps and never reused, even when two users open
claims at the same moment. A draft has no number, and voiding a claim clears its number (the
number is not given to anyone else). Show the number on the claim. Every audit line about a
claim that has a number gains number=<number> at its end (so CLAIM_OPENED and CLAIM_SETTLED
carry it; a CLAIM_VOIDED line carries the number the claim had).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims now get a number when they're opened, and `bin/e2e` passes. The audit file from that run shows the right numbers: opened 1, then voided (the voided line still says `number=1`), then opened 2, and the two claims opened at the same moment by different users got 3 and 4.

**How it works**
- **Stored data** (new migration `V8__claim_number.sql`): each sheet keeps the last number it gave out (`sheet.claim_numbers`), and each claim has a `claim_number` that's empty for drafts. A unique index on (sheet, number) is a backstop so two claims on a sheet can never share a number.
- **Opening a claim** (`OpenClaim`): the server adds one to the sheet's counter in the same transaction that opens the claim. That locks the sheet's row until the change commits, so claims opened at the same moment are numbered one after the other. If the open is refused, the counter change is undone too, so no gaps appear. After taking the lock it re-reads the claim's saved status, so if the same claim is opened twice at once, the second attempt is refused instead of using up a second number.
- **Voiding a claim** (`VoidClaim`): the claim's number is cleared and never given out again. The number it had is passed along so the `CLAIM_VOIDED` line can still show it.
- **Audit lines**: any claim line, when the claim has a number, ends with `number=<n>` after the existing fields. That covers opened and settled, and edited too if an open claim is edited. Drafts get nothing extra.
- **Screen**: the server now returns the number with each claim, and each claim row shows it in a new `claim-number` cell, which is empty for drafts and voided claims.

Any `OPEN` or `SETTLED` claims already in a store before this migration would have no number. That doesn't matter while the database is the in-memory one that starts fresh each time, but they'd need filling in if the data were ever kept between runs.
